title: Choose Snippi's visual world (safer hand)
question: The familiar end of the spectrum: three grounded directions and the category standard. Pick one.

options.label: Swiss Grid
options.lineage: International Typographic Style: Müller-Brockmann posters and Swiss corporate manuals
options.thesis: Precision as luxury: one heavy grotesk, a strict grid, and the code panel treated as the photograph.
materials: one heavy grotesk at huge scale
flat signal red used only for actions
code panels cropped square like photographs
options.viewport: A huge flush-left headline over most of the screen width, with a large real snippet panel pinned to the grid's right columns and one red sign-up button. Dark theme inverts to near-black with the same red.
options.risk: Reads as generic minimalism if the scale contrast is timid; it depends on type set really large and spacing kept strict.

options.label: The Reference Manual
options.lineage: Cloth-bound programming references and their running heads, margins and marginalia
options.thesis: Your library as a well-made reference book: each snippet an entry with its own head, note and code.
materials: navy book cloth with a blind-stamped title
an oxblood ribbon marker as the accent
options.viewport: A navy cloth cover field holding the Snippi title, opening to a two-page spread: an entry heading and description on the left page, the code on the right.
options.risk: Book paper drifts toward the cream-and-serif look generated sites default to, and a spread layout is harder to make work on phones.

options.label: Label Maker
options.lineage: Embossed Dymo label tape on drawers, cables and toolboxes
options.thesis: Name it, stick it on, find it later: every snippet title is a strip of embossed tape.
materials: raised plastic label tape in black, red and blue
options.viewport: The headline punched out as three strips of tape across the screen, with the sign-up button as a red strip and a live demo where you type a title and watch it emboss.
options.risk: The most playful of the three; done loudly it reads as a novelty gimmick rather than premium.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Developer-tool SaaS at the craft level of Linear, Raycast and Vercel.
materials: large crops of the real dashboard and editor
canonCard.viewport: Tight headline and sign-up button over a large crop of the real Snippi dashboard and editor, with short sections that each show one real interface fragment.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other developer tool by design.
